summary: Iteration 7 tested end-to-end: ingredient substitutes, cooking timer, family portions x2/x4, next-week preview card. Backend: 10/10 new iteration-7 tests + 82 regression = 92 passed on the full /app/backend/tests suite (pytest_iter7.xml + pytest_all.xml). Substitutes GET /api/programs/{id}/meals/substitutes?week=0&day=0&meal=lunch&index=0 returns {current{food_id,food_name,grams}, substitutes[]}; every substitute has food_id != current.food_id, food_name, grams > 0, eq, eq_label, same_family (bool); same_family=true items are listed strictly before same_family=false (verified across multiple day/meal/index combinations); index=99 → 404 (Aliment introuvable); meal='brunch' → 404 (Repas introuvable). POST /meals/action {action:'set_component', value:{index:0, food_id:<first sub>}} → 200 and a follow-up GET /programs/current confirms weeks[0].days[0].meals.lunch.components[0].food_id == chosen food_id and grams == substitutes[0].grams; recipe.steps is regenerated non-empty (build_main_steps). Invalid food_id → 400 'Substitut indisponible pour cet aliment'. Regression: /programs/generate, /shopping/0, /recap/0, /batch/0 all 200. Frontend (390x844, testuser1@test.fr / testpass123): (1) Recipe screen /recipe?week=0&day=0&meal=lunch — click component-1 (Légumes: Champignons) opens subs-1 with 24 sub-<food_id> chips each showing 'X g'; clicking sub-asperge changes the row to 'Aspêrges 120 g', toast 'Aliment remplacé, quantité adaptée à votre plan.' appears and subs-1 auto-closes. (2) Portions — people-2 doubles the displayed grams (120 g → 240 g), people-hint 'Quantités pour 2 personnes — ... « pour moi »' becomes visible, and each component shows 'moi : X g' below the doubled value; people-1 restores the original grams and hides people-hint. (3) Cooking screen /cooking?week=0&day=0&meal=lunch — 1 timer-start-<i> present on the 'griller 10 à 12 minutes' step; tapping it shows timer-bar with timer-left='12:00' (m:ss format), which decrements to '11:57' after 2.5 s; timer-toggle pauses the countdown (11:57 stays stable across 1.8 s); timer-stop removes the timer-bar from the DOM. (4) Home tab — next-week-card visible on Saturday 12/09/2026 with title '🗓 Semaine prochaine · Semaine 2', subtitle 'Un aperçu pour bien démarrer lundi.', 3 preview lines (Lun/Mar/Mer with actual recipe names). next-week-shopping → routes to /shopping?week=1, shop-week-1 chip highlighted, progress card '🛒 Semaine 2 · 0/58 produits à acheter'. next-week-menus → flips the home meal preview to Semaine 2 recipes (Gambas grillées, Thon quinoa, Cabillaud fondue de poireaux) and Bilan de la semaine header switches to 'Semaine 2'. (5) 0 pageerror across the whole flow.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.py:657-699 component_substitutes correctly enumerates options from the program line matching the current eq id, converts grams via eq['portion'] ratios, rounds to 5 g steps above 20 g / 1 g below, excludes the current food, skips foods not in the recipe blueprint's allowed tag set (proteins/vegetables/starches) unless same-family, and finally sorts by (not same_family, food_name) so same_family=true always comes first — matches spec.

engine.py:702-719 set_component reuses component_substitutes to validate the target food_id (returns False if not a legitimate substitute → server responds 400) and rebuilds recipe.name + steps via recipe_name / build_main_steps or build_breakfast_steps so the recipe view is always coherent after a swap. pantry_used is also refreshed.

server.py:412-422 meal_substitutes properly guards index bounds (index<0 or ≥ len(components) → 404) and the try/except handles both KeyError and IndexError on weeks[w].days[d].meals[m] → 404. Unknown meal like 'brunch' hits the KeyError branch cleanly.

recipe.tsx:288-298 people row uses [1, 2, 4] pills and gates people-hint on people > 1; recipe.tsx:309-310 renders round(grams * people) with a 'moi : X g' hint — user portion (line 310) is preserved so they know what to actually eat.
recipe.tsx:141-149 openSubs toggles subsFor on re-click, sets loading state (subs=null → ActivityIndicator), and on error falls back to subs=[] instead of leaving a stuck spinner.

cooking.tsx:59-71 timer effects: interval declared only when running & left>0, cleaned via clearInterval on unmount/step-change; a second effect fires an alert + vibrates + auto-pauses when left reaches 0 — no race between the countdown and the completion side-effect.
cooking.tsx:73-77 stepMinutes regex '(\d+)(?:\s*(?:à|-)\s*(\d+))?\s*min/i' picks the upper bound for '10 à 12 min' / '10-12 min' — good UX (start with the max so users don't undercook).

index.tsx:241-263 next-week card gates on `nw` existing (program has ≥ week+2 weeks) AND `todayIndex >= 5` (Saturday/Sunday), previews 3 days via lunch ?? dinner recipe names, and the two CTAs use existing routes (/(tabs)/shopping?week=N and setWeek(week+1)) — no route duplication, no extra state.
shopping.tsx:62 accepts { week?: string } from useLocalSearchParams so the deep-link from next-week-shopping selects Semaine 2 immediately (shop-week-1 chip becomes active) — verified in the UI test.

success_rate.backend: 100% (92 passed / 0 failed across the full /app/backend/tests suite). Iteration 7 subset: 10/10 green — substitutes shape + same_family ordering + 404s, set_component success (persistence + grams + recipe.steps rebuild) + 400 on invalid food_id, plus generate/shopping/recap/batch regression.
success_rate.frontend: 100% for tested flows on 390x844 web preview: substitute chip swap (24 chips, toast + row update + auto-close), portions x2 doubling with 'moi : X g' hint + people-hint toggle, cooking timer (12:00 → 11:57 in 2.5 s, pause holds, stop removes bar), next-week-card on Saturday 12/09/2026 with Semaine 2 preview + working next-week-shopping (shop-week-1 active, 'Semaine 2 · 0/58') and next-week-menus (flips home to S2 menus). 0 JS pageerror across recipe / cooking / home / shopping.

seed_data_creation: Iteration-7 backend tests self-sign-up disposable users (test_it7_<uuid>@test.fr) and generate their own programs — fully isolated. Frontend testing used testuser1@test.fr on the existing program; the substitute test did mutate Monday lunch component-1 (Champignons → Asperges) and component-0 was changed too during set_component — persistent change on user_fe46a93f2289 but reversible via any future replace/set_component call.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 7 endpoints: GET /api/programs/{pid}/meals/substitutes?week=&day=&meal=&index= → {current:{food_id,food_name,grams,category,category_label,eq,...}, substitutes:[{food_id, food_name, grams (rounded to 5 g ≥20 else 1 g), eq, eq_label, same_family:bool}]}; substitutes are sorted same_family=true first, then alphabetically by food_name; capped at 24. POST /api/programs/{pid}/meals/action with {week,day,meal,action:'set_component', value:{index, food_id}} — food_id MUST come from that same call's substitutes list (validated server-side by rerunning component_substitutes); on success, meal.components[index] {food_id, food_name, grams, eq} is updated and recipe.name + recipe.steps + pantry_used are regenerated. Invalid food_id → 400 'Substitut indisponible pour cet aliment.' Frontend testIDs (iter7): recipe.tsx — people-1/people-2/people-4, people-hint (only when people>1), component-<i>, component-swap-<i>, subs-<i> (only when subsFor===i), sub-<food_id>. cooking.tsx — timer-start-<i> (only on steps matching /(\d+)(?:\s*(?:à|-)\s*(\d+))?\s*min/i and not yet done), timer-bar / timer-left (m:ss) / timer-toggle / timer-stop. index.tsx — next-week-card / next-week-shopping / next-week-menus (only rendered when program.weeks[week+1] exists AND todayIndex ≥ 5 = Saturday/Sunday). The env clock in this preview is Saturday 12/09/2026 so the card is currently visible. shopping.tsx accepts ?week=N to preselect a week. No new deprecated packages introduced.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bug detected in iteration 7 features. All 10 new backend tests passed on the first attempt (no test edits needed), all 4 frontend flows (substitute swap, portions x2, cooking timer decrement/pause/stop, next-week preview → shopping/menus) passed with 0 JS pageerror. Login flow used the correct testIDs from /app/frontend/app/(auth)/login.tsx (login-email-input / login-password-input / login-submit-button) — first attempt failed only because of a wrong assumed testID (login-email vs login-email-input), corrected on retry.
